newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Country Road says 1st qtr sales lower.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Country Road says 1st qtr sales lower.

text.p: Upmarket fashion house Country Road Ltd said on Thursday its sales in the first quarter ending October had fallen quite substantially when compared with those of a year ago.
"Retail conditions remain most difficult in Australia. Sales have fallen away quite substantially in this quarter," chairman Bill Loewenthal told the annual meeting of shareholders.
He did not provide specific figures.
Chief executive officer Mike Howell later told reporters that the clothing side of the business had suffered more than its homeware operations in the latest three months.
He said the upcoming Christmas period was a key time for the company, which was well-stocked.
Howell said he was confident the company's product mix was better than last year's.

"We are very confident about Christmas. We just hope that consumer sentiment indicators ... will reflect itself in a real upturn in sales," Howell said. Country Road was considering the opening of three to five new stores in the United States, but this division was unlikely to make a profit in 1996/97, he said.
U.S. chief executive Michael Warner told Reuters last month that the likely expansion would be based in the northeastern region where Country Road already has a solid customer base.
Country Road had a net profit of A$10.17 million in the year to July 28 from A$15.89 million a year earlier.
